Title: Indian 5 pc broken rice prices may rise by USD 60 per tonne amid freight costs, global supply risks: IREF
Description: Indian 5 per cent broken rice prices could increase by around USD 60 per metric tonne amid international freight costs and changing global market conditions, although such increases may not be sustainable over the longer term, according to Dev Garg, Vice President of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation (IREF). Speaking during the first knowledge session, "Global Rice Demand and Supply Outlook 2027," at the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026 in New Delhi, Garg highlighted the role of international freight costs in determining the competitiveness and pricing of Indian rice in global markets. He noted that the impact of geopolitical conflicts on rice prices would largely depend on freight costs and prevailing market conditions, cautioning that price increases driven by these factors could face sustainability challenges. The conference highlighted that the global rice market in 2027 would be influenced by weather risks, production and consumption trends, stock levels, government policies, currency movements and changing buyer behaviour. Experts identified the potential development of El Nino as a major supply-side risk, warning that adverse weather conditions could affect rice production across successive growing cycles in Asia. Indonesia and Vietnam were identified as countries facing significant exposure to weather-related production risks, while India and the Philippines could also experience disruptions, particularly in rabi and second-crop production. Experts stressed the importance of monitoring El Nino developments through early 2027, as these could influence global rice availability, exportable surpluses and price volatility. On the demand side, the session indicated that South Asia and Africa would account for all growth in global rice demand during 2026-27, highlighting their increasing importance in international rice trade. Vietnam was identified as an emerging second-largest rice importer globally, while the Philippines continued to remain an important importing market. Experts also discussed the possibility of higher rice import requirements from Indonesia if El Nino-related weather disruptions affect domestic production. Meanwhile, an audience poll conducted during the session indicated that a bullish scenario was the preferred outlook for the global rice market in 2027. However, experts cautioned that the direction of rice prices would depend on the evolving balance between production, consumption, stocks and international trade requirements. The conference emphasised that Indian rice exporters must closely monitor freight rates, weather developments and shifting import demand to remain competitive in international markets. (ANI)

Title: RBI's Rs 2.5 lakh crore liquidity infusion raises questions over tightening policy signal: SBI Report
Description: The Reserve Bank of India's decision to inject Rs 2.5 lakh crore into the banking system through repo auctions has raised questions over its liquidity management approach, even as the central bank has adopted a tighter monetary policy stance to address inflation concerns, according to a report by the State Bank of India (SBI). In its Ecowrap report, SBI said the RBI had sent a clear and consistent message on monetary tightening through its policy resolution, the Governor's statement and the MPC minutes. However, it questioned the rationale behind injecting liquidity while the central bank was pursuing a calibrated tightening approach. "We, however, find it a little difficult to understand the reasons behind the RBI's move to inject liquidity through repo auctions of Rs 2.5 lakh crores even as the primary objective is to ensure that the RBI is in a 'calibrated tightening' mode and the RBI Governor also emphasising less on liquidity in the October policy," the report said. SBI noted that the RBI had moved the operating rate to the upper end of the policy corridor, describing it as an appropriate signal during a tightening cycle. However, it said the liquidity infusion appeared difficult to reconcile with the central bank's emphasis on controlling inflation. The report also pointed to the RBI's decision to cancel all Treasury bill auctions, suggesting that markets could interpret the measures as attempts to fine-tune movements in bond yields. Despite these steps, SBI expects Indian government bond yields to remain elevated. The report said yields were unlikely to decline even as US Treasury yields had fallen below 5 per cent, citing expectations of elevated crude oil prices and developments in global bond markets. SBI said the spread between Indian government securities and US Treasury yields had reached 250 basis points and was moving towards normalisation. It added that elevated crude oil prices could prevent domestic yields from declining. The report also highlighted the RBI's changing emphasis in its assessment of economic risks. According to SBI, the October MPC minutes placed greater emphasis on external conditions and financial stability than the August minutes, while giving less emphasis to liquidity and monetary policy transmission. SBI said this reflected the RBI's increased awareness of threats to external stability arising from widening geopolitical conflicts, even as inflation concerns remained central to the decision to tighten monetary policy. On the broader policy approach, SBI argued that the RBI should avoid managing liquidity through simultaneous injections and withdrawals. "We believe, while concerns on financial stability may have played a part, but it is better for RBI to stay away from two-way liquidity management policy of both injection and withdrawal simultaneously," the report said. Instead, SBI continued to advocate widening the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor, arguing that it could act as an automatic stabiliser during periods of uncertainty. (ANI)

Description: Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov expressed confidence on Friday that bilateral relations with India are progressing towards higher levels, noting expanding prospects across energy sectors, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and logistical corridors, while characterising External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar's official trip to Baku as a very valuable meeting. Following his meeting with EAM Jaishankar in the Azerbaijani capital, Bayramov described the exchange as comprehensive, constructive and highly productive, addressing various bilateral, regional and global issues. Furthermore, Bayramov pointed to energy, agricultural cooperation and pharmaceutical collaboration as key growth areas, alongside major transit networks connecting eastern, western, northern and southern corridors, leveraging Azerbaijan's strategic geographical location. Concerning cultural and interpersonal connections, Bayramov reported that two direct flight routes operated between Baku and Delhi, approximately 500 Indian scholars had enrolled in Azerbaijani higher education institutions this year, and over 30 Indian cinematic productions had utilised local backdrops in recent years. The two foreign ministers additionally evaluated geopolitical conditions within the South Caucasus, encompassing peace and normalisation efforts between Armenia and Azerbaijan, escalating frictions in the Middle East and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, according to Bayramov. We believe that this visit and the discussions that we have had on the various issues will have a good impact on the development of the bilateral relationship between our two nations, Bayramov stated, according to the English translation of his remarks. Title: "Maintenance of peace in border area essential": MEA clarifies position on reported face-offs with PLA in Arunachal
Description: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday clarified the government's position after DG ITBP Shatrujeet Kapoor was reported to have spoken of continuing PLA face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh. The MEA in its briefing on Friday said, Insofar as the specifics are concerned, I would refer you to the Ministry of Defence. As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control. The two sides have also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas for better border management. I would also like to emphasise that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations. The clarification comes amidst a political firestorm over the purported remarks by the ITBP DG. Congress President Malikarjun Kharge took the fight to the Prime Minister demanding that he come clean on the subject. Asking specific questions Kharge said, The ITBP DG's confirmation of continuing PLA face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh is deeply alarming. After Doklam and Galwan, is another serious confrontation unfolding? Reports of Chinese incursions near Taksing emerged in August. Yet, even 47 days after Corps Commander-level talks at Wacha-Damai, reportedly just 180 km away, confrontations continue. Has India's patrolling access been compromised? Arunachal Pradesh is an inseparable part of India. Why is the nation being kept in the dark? The Congress President also demanded accountability on the diplomatic front and called on the PM to address Parliament on the issue. At least 23 reported Modi-Xi meetings and interactions, 25 Special Representatives' rounds involving NSA Ajit Doval, 36 WMCC meetings, and successive SCO and BRICS Summits. What tangible results have these engagements delivered? Have India's pre-May 2020 patrolling rights been fully restored? Our Armed Forces have our complete confidence. But National security demands accountability, not diplomatic photo opportunities & Hugplomacy! Instead of attacking the Opposition, PM Modi must take Parliament and the Nation into confidence, Kharge said. On August 25 this year, the 25th Round of Talks between the Special Representatives (SR) of India and China on the Boundary Question was held in Beijing. The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to uphold the guidance received from the leaders of the two countries, maintain peace and tranquillity in the border areas and create an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations. The two sides also underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution. The two sides further agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commanderlevel meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. (ANI)

Title: Indian 5 pc broken rice prices may rise by USD 60 per tonne amid freight costs, global supply risks: IREF
Description: Indian 5 per cent broken rice prices could increase by around USD 60 per metric tonne amid international freight costs and changing global market conditions, although such increases may not be sustainable over the longer term, according to Dev Garg, Vice President of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation (IREF). Speaking during the first knowledge session, "Global Rice Demand and Supply Outlook 2027," at the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026 in New Delhi, Garg highlighted the role of international freight costs in determining the competitiveness and pricing of Indian rice in global markets. He noted that the impact of geopolitical conflicts on rice prices would largely depend on freight costs and prevailing market conditions, cautioning that price increases driven by these factors could face sustainability challenges. The conference highlighted that the global rice market in 2027 would be influenced by weather risks, production and consumption trends, stock levels, government policies, currency movements and changing buyer behaviour. Experts identified the potential development of El Nino as a major supply-side risk, warning that adverse weather conditions could affect rice production across successive growing cycles in Asia. Indonesia and Vietnam were identified as countries facing significant exposure to weather-related production risks, while India and the Philippines could also experience disruptions, particularly in rabi and second-crop production. Experts stressed the importance of monitoring El Nino developments through early 2027, as these could influence global rice availability, exportable surpluses and price volatility. On the demand side, the session indicated that South Asia and Africa would account for all growth in global rice demand during 2026-27, highlighting their increasing importance in international rice trade. Vietnam was identified as an emerging second-largest rice importer globally, while the Philippines continued to remain an important importing market. Experts also discussed the possibility of higher rice import requirements from Indonesia if El Nino-related weather disruptions affect domestic production. Meanwhile, an audience poll conducted during the session indicated that a bullish scenario was the preferred outlook for the global rice market in 2027. However, experts cautioned that the direction of rice prices would depend on the evolving balance between production, consumption, stocks and international trade requirements. The conference emphasised that Indian rice exporters must closely monitor freight rates, weather developments and shifting import demand to remain competitive in international markets. (ANI)

Title: RBI's Rs 2.5 lakh crore liquidity infusion raises questions over tightening policy signal: SBI Report
Description: The Reserve Bank of India's decision to inject Rs 2.5 lakh crore into the banking system through repo auctions has raised questions over its liquidity management approach, even as the central bank has adopted a tighter monetary policy stance to address inflation concerns, according to a report by the State Bank of India (SBI). In its Ecowrap report, SBI said the RBI had sent a clear and consistent message on monetary tightening through its policy resolution, the Governor's statement and the MPC minutes. However, it questioned the rationale behind injecting liquidity while the central bank was pursuing a calibrated tightening approach. "We, however, find it a little difficult to understand the reasons behind the RBI's move to inject liquidity through repo auctions of Rs 2.5 lakh crores even as the primary objective is to ensure that the RBI is in a 'calibrated tightening' mode and the RBI Governor also emphasising less on liquidity in the October policy," the report said. SBI noted that the RBI had moved the operating rate to the upper end of the policy corridor, describing it as an appropriate signal during a tightening cycle. However, it said the liquidity infusion appeared difficult to reconcile with the central bank's emphasis on controlling inflation. The report also pointed to the RBI's decision to cancel all Treasury bill auctions, suggesting that markets could interpret the measures as attempts to fine-tune movements in bond yields. Despite these steps, SBI expects Indian government bond yields to remain elevated. The report said yields were unlikely to decline even as US Treasury yields had fallen below 5 per cent, citing expectations of elevated crude oil prices and developments in global bond markets. SBI said the spread between Indian government securities and US Treasury yields had reached 250 basis points and was moving towards normalisation. It added that elevated crude oil prices could prevent domestic yields from declining. The report also highlighted the RBI's changing emphasis in its assessment of economic risks. On the broader policy approach, SBI argued that the RBI should avoid managing liquidity through simultaneous injections and withdrawals. "We believe, while concerns on financial stability may have played a part, but it is better for RBI to stay away from two-way liquidity management policy of both injection and withdrawal simultaneously," the report said. Title: French Open: PV Sindhu beats Chiu Pin-chian to enter semi-finals
Description: Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu kept India's campaign alive at the French Open 2026 badminton tournament after defeating Chinese Taipei's Chiu Pin-chian in straight games to enter the women's singles semi-finals on Friday. The world No. 11 Indian shuttler defeated world No. 17 Chiu 21-13, 21-14 at the Arena Grand Paris in a quarter-final encounter that lasted 39 minutes, according to Olympics.com. Sindhu dominated proceedings from the outset, taking an 11-5 lead at the interval in the opening game before comfortably closing it out. She carried the momentum into the second game, racing to a 7-0 advantage and maintaining her control to seal the match. The victory marked Sindhu's second win over Chiu, having also defeated the Chinese Taipei shuttler at the Asian Games 2026 last month. Sindhu has now reached the semi-finals of four BWF World Tour tournaments this year. She previously made the last four at the Malaysia Open in January and the Australian Badminton Open in June, before winning the Japan Open title in July. The Indian will face either Indonesia's world championships bronze medallist Putri Kusuma Wardani or Japan's Hina Akechi in the semi-finals on Saturday. Sindhu remains India's only contender at the BWF Super 750 tournament after Ashmita Chaliha bowed out in the quarter-finals earlier on Friday. Chaliha, who had stunned three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi in the pre-quarter-finals to register the biggest win of her career, went down 21-10, 17-21, 21-16 against Japan's Olympic medallist Nozomi Okuhara, according to Olympics.com. India's men's singles campaign had ended on Thursday after Ayush Shetty retired hurt, while Lakshya Sen withdrew before his opening-round match. The Indian men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, along with the women's doubles combination of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, had also suffered opening-round exits. (ANI)

Title: Indian 5 pc broken rice prices may rise by USD 60 per tonne amid freight costs, global supply risks: IREF
Description: Indian 5 per cent broken rice prices could increase by around USD 60 per metric tonne amid international freight costs and changing global market conditions, although such increases may not be sustainable over the longer term, according to Dev Garg, Vice President of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation (IREF). Speaking during the first knowledge session, "Global Rice Demand and Supply Outlook 2027," at the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026 in New Delhi, Garg highlighted the role of international freight costs in determining the competitiveness and pricing of Indian rice in global markets. He noted that the impact of geopolitical conflicts on rice prices would largely depend on freight costs and prevailing market conditions, cautioning that price increases driven by these factors could face sustainability challenges. The conference highlighted that the global rice market in 2027 would be influenced by weather risks, production and consumption trends, stock levels, government policies, currency movements and changing buyer behaviour. Experts identified the potential development of El Nino as a major supply-side risk, warning that adverse weather conditions could affect rice production across successive growing cycles in Asia. Indonesia and Vietnam were identified as countries facing significant exposure to weather-related production risks, while India and the Philippines could also experience disruptions, particularly in rabi and second-crop production. Experts stressed the importance of monitoring El Nino developments through early 2027, as these could influence global rice availability, exportable surpluses and price volatility. On the demand side, the session indicated that South Asia and Africa would account for all growth in global rice demand during 2026-27, highlighting their increasing importance in international rice trade. Vietnam was identified as an emerging second-largest rice importer globally, while the Philippines continued to remain an important importing market. Experts also discussed the possibility of higher rice import requirements from Indonesia if El Nino-related weather disruptions affect domestic production. Meanwhile, an audience poll conducted during the session indicated that a bullish scenario was the preferred outlook for the global rice market in 2027. However, experts cautioned that the direction of rice prices would depend on the evolving balance between production, consumption, stocks and international trade requirements. The conference emphasised that Indian rice exporters must closely monitor freight rates, weather developments and shifting import demand to remain competitive in international markets. (ANI)

Title: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal calls SMFCL's role vital to propel India's maritime growth under PM Modi's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047
Description: Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, inaugurated the corporate office of Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL) at the Institute for Studies in Industrial Development (ISID) in New Delhi on Friday, giving a permanent home to what he called India's first dedicated Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) in the maritime sector. The new office opens at a time of fast progress. As of September 30, SMFCL has sanctioned Rs 11,563 crore of financing and disbursed Rs 5,107 crore, with more than half of the sanctioned amount still to be drawn as projects advance. The corporation's plan looks well beyond today. It aims to reach cumulative disbursements of Rs 60,205 crore by the end of FY2031, a build-up that depends on equity support to scale up in line with RBI norms and its debt-to-equity ratio. As India's first dedicated NBFC in the maritime sector, SMFCL is playing a pivotal role in mobilising long-term finance for port-led development, enhancing shipbuilding and coastal connectivity and catalysing the overall growth of our maritime economy. It has a vital role to play in propelling India's maritime growth towards achieving the vision of PM Narendra Modi of becoming a leading maritime nation of the world by 2047, Sarbananda Sonowal said. The Maritime Development Fund (MDF), which has two components, is also taking shape. For its MIF component, SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed official Fund Manager. Registration as an Alternative Investment Fund with SEBI is due to be completed by the end of November, and the first close of Rs 5,000 crore is targeted by January 2027. The Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) is already delivering. Its online portal, www.iifmdf.in, is live, and loans of Rs 4,500 crore have been supported so far. About Rs 25 crore of interest subvention has been released against interest paid by borrowers. Under PM Narendra Modi's transformative Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, India is building a stronger, more self-reliant and globally competitive maritime sector, Sonowal said. The schemes SMFCL runs now cover a maritime project from first idea to final loan. The Government of India's contribution to the Maritime Investment Fund, up to Rs 9,800 crore, is channelled through SMFCL, while SBI Ventures, selected as Fund Manager, brings professional management to the fund. The Interest Incentivisation Fund eases the cost of borrowing for eligible shipyards, with SMFCL working out the incentive, running the application and claims portal, and releasing the interest support. Under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, the credit risk cover corpus is managed centrally and backed by premium and claims review, giving shipyards and lenders a safety net against payment risk. SMFCL's own lending appraises, sanctions and monitors projects across ports, rail and road links, inland waterways, coastal infrastructure, port-hinterland logistics, shipbuilding and ship repair. It also oversees the release and use of Sagarmala and National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC) funds, so that money reaches projects and is tracked until it is spent. (ANI)

Title: Indian 5 pc broken rice prices may rise by USD 60 per tonne amid freight costs, global supply risks: IREF
Description: Indian 5 per cent broken rice prices could increase by around USD 60 per metric tonne amid international freight costs and changing global market conditions, although such increases may not be sustainable over the longer term, according to Dev Garg, Vice President of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation (IREF). Speaking during the first knowledge session, "Global Rice Demand and Supply Outlook 2027," at the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026 in New Delhi, Garg highlighted the role of international freight costs in determining the competitiveness and pricing of Indian rice in global markets. He noted that the impact of geopolitical conflicts on rice prices would largely depend on freight costs and prevailing market conditions, cautioning that price increases driven by these factors could face sustainability challenges. The conference highlighted that the global rice market in 2027 would be influenced by weather risks, production and consumption trends, stock levels, government policies, currency movements and changing buyer behaviour. Experts identified the potential development of El Nino as a major supply-side risk, warning that adverse weather conditions could affect rice production across successive growing cycles in Asia. Indonesia and Vietnam were identified as countries facing significant exposure to weather-related production risks, while India and the Philippines could also experience disruptions, particularly in rabi and second-crop production. Experts stressed the importance of monitoring El Nino developments through early 2027, as these could influence global rice availability, exportable surpluses and price volatility. On the demand side, the session indicated that South Asia and Africa would account for all growth in global rice demand during 2026-27, highlighting their increasing importance in international rice trade. Vietnam was identified as an emerging second-largest rice importer globally, while the Philippines continued to remain an important importing market. Experts also discussed the possibility of higher rice import requirements from Indonesia if El Nino-related weather disruptions affect domestic production. Meanwhile, an audience poll conducted during the session indicated that a bullish scenario was the preferred outlook for the global rice market in 2027. However, experts cautioned that the direction of rice prices would depend on the evolving balance between production, consumption, stocks and international trade requirements. The conference emphasised that Indian rice exporters must closely monitor freight rates, weather developments and shifting import demand to remain competitive in international markets. (ANI)

Title: Final polls show Netanyahu and opposition blocs short of majority ahead of Israel election: Israeli media
Description: The final opinion polls published ahead of Israel's national election next week indicate continued political deadlock, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's governing coalition nor the opposition-led change bloc projected to secure the 61 seats required for a majority in the Knesset, according to The Times of Israel. The surveys, aired by Israeli television channels on Friday, forecast that several smaller parties would fail to cross the electoral threshold, potentially narrowing the options for forming a governing coalition after Tuesday's vote. According to The Times of Israel, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party is projected to emerge as the largest faction in two of the three surveys, ahead of Netanyahu's Likud. Yoaz Hendel's Reservists party is forecast to enter the Knesset in only one of the three polls, while Ofer Winter's People of Israel party is projected to fall short in all three. A Channel 13 poll predicted that the change bloc would win 54 seats, compared with 50 for parties loyal to Netanyahu, while predominantly Arab parties would secure 16 seats. The survey projected 22 seats for Yashar, 19 for Likud, 14 for Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad and 10 for the left-wing Democrats. The Joint List was forecast to win nine seats, while Yisrael Beytenu, Otzma Yehudit, United Torah Judaism and Religious Zionism were each projected to secure eight seats. Shas and Ra'am were forecast to win seven seats apiece. The poll also indicated that the parties led by Winter, Hendel and Moti Leitner would fail to enter the Knesset. A Channel 12 survey projected 56 seats for the change bloc and 50 for the governing coalition, with the Joint List and Ra'am together securing 14 seats. The poll gave Yashar 23 seats, Likud 21, B'Yachad 15 and the Democrats 10. The Joint List was projected to win nine seats, while Yisrael Beytenu, Shas and Otzma Yehudit were each forecast to secure eight. United Torah Judaism was projected to win seven seats, Religious Zionism six and Ra'am five. Like the Channel 13 survey, the Channel 12 poll predicted that the parties led by Winter, Hendel and Leitner would fail to cross the electoral threshold. A poll by public broadcaster Kan offered a slightly different picture, projecting 52 seats for the change bloc, 50 for Netanyahu's coalition and 14 for the Arab parties. Hendel's Reservists party was forecast to enter the Knesset with four seats. The Kan survey projected 22 seats for Yashar, 20 for Likud and 14 for B'Yachad. The Joint List was forecast to win nine seats, while the Democrats, Otzma Yehudit, Yisrael Beytenu and United Torah Judaism were each projected to secure eight seats. Shas and Religious Zionism were forecast to win seven seats each, while Ra'am was projected to get five. Winter's People of Israel party and Leitner's Charedi Public party were also projected to fall short in the Kan poll. The Times of Israel reported that the surveys were published on Friday before a ban on releasing election polls came into effect on Saturday. Exit polls are expected to be released when polling stations close at 10 pm on Tuesday. The Channel 13 survey, conducted by pollsters Shmuel Rosner and Noah Slepkov, included 1,875 respondents and had a margin of error of 2.3 per cent. The Channel 12 poll, conducted by Midgam's Manu Geva, surveyed 1,018 respondents and had a 4.4 per cent margin of error. Kan's survey, conducted by Dudu Hasid of the Kantar Institute, included 1,106 respondents and had a 3 per cent margin of error. The surveys followed a final pre-election poll published by Zman Yisrael, The Times of Israel's sister site, which projected 51 seats each for the two Jewish-led blocs, 14 for Arab-led parties and four for Reservists. With neither major bloc projected to reach the 61-seat majority, forming a government could depend on parties reconsidering campaign pledges not to join forces with certain factions. The Times of Israel reported that if no governing coalition can be formed, repeat elections could be held in early 2027, with Netanyahu remaining caretaker prime minister in the interim. The Israeli polls come at a time when Israel Defence Forces on Friday (local time) said that it has launched a "limited counterterrorism" operation in the Hebron area following the killing of two of its soldiers in a shooting attack. In a post on X, IDF said, "In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell, and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged." IDF said troops have begun conducting precise searches throughout the area to locate and dismantle terrorist infrastructure and weapons, while questioning suspects. It further cautioned that residents living in the area where forces are operating will be able to leave through 3 designated exit points. "Following questioning and security screening. Individuals who raise suspicion during the screening process will be referred to security forces for further questioning," IDF said. Earlier on Friday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had visited Hebron after ordering a "full lockdown" of the West Bank following a "terror attack" in the area that left five people wounded in an assault by alleged Hamas militants, just five days before Israel goes to the polls. (ANI)

Title: Quantum computing could generate up to USD 2.7 trillion in economic value by 2035: McKinsey
Description: Quantum computing could generate between USD 1.3 trillion and USD 2.7 trillion in economic value worldwide by 2035, but businesses need to invest in talent, technology and partnerships now to secure an early advantage, according to a report by McKinsey & Company. The report said quantum technology was moving from experimental projects towards commercial applications, with more than 300 organisations worldwide already working with quantum technology providers. The report warned that companies delaying investment risk losing access to the partnerships, talent and intellectual property needed to compete as the technology develops. It also highlighted potential security risks, as sufficiently advanced quantum computers could eventually break the public-key encryption systems used to protect sensitive information. "Waiting to invest is risky," the report said, adding that companies could face serious security challenges when quantum computers reach the stage of being able to break existing encryption methods. McKinsey outlined three stages of development, from early commercial adoption to the establishment of competitive positions by 2035 and a wider quantum-enabled economy by 2040. Investment in the sector is already increasing. Equity investment in quantum technology rose from USD 2.5 billion in 2024 to USD 13.3 billion in 2025, the report said. Combined revenue of quantum computing companies crossed USD 1 billion in 2025 and could rise to as much as USD 4.4 billion by 2028. The report estimated that the global market for quantum computing hardware, software and services could reach USD 60 billion to USD 100 billion by 2035. Quantum communication could represent a market worth USD 11 billion to USD 15 billion, while quantum sensing could reach USD 7 billion to USD 10 billion by the same year. However, McKinsey cautioned that the timeline remains uncertain because of manufacturing constraints, shortages of specialised talent and a lack of consensus on which quantum computing technology will scale most effectively. The report also identified cybersecurity, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and robotics as areas where quantum technology could create significant value. Quantum computing could generate up to USD 400 billion in value for the pharmaceutical industry and unlock up to USD 800 billion in the chemicals industry by 2035, it estimated. McKinsey further said businesses should focus on building partnerships, testing potential applications and developing internal expertise before large-scale quantum systems become commercially available. It added that quantum computing could also help address computing and energy constraints affecting the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI). (ANI)

The report suggested that Beijing may be using pressure against family members to discourage politicians and activists from engaging in activities associated with Taiwanese independence. As reported by The Taipei Times, one recent example involves sanctions against VWAY, a company owned by Shen Tu-cheng, the father of Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) legislator and Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. China's Taiwan Affairs Office announced restrictions barring the company from conducting business with Chinese organisations, enterprises and individuals, the Taipei Times reported. Puma Shen was included in Beijing's list of around a dozen people designated as "diehard separatists" in October 2024. According to the report, those named could face severe punishment, including the death penalty, under Beijing's interpretation of its Anti-Secession Law. The report also highlighted other alleged cases of pressure on relatives of Taiwanese public figures. Robert Tsao, founder of United Microelectronics Corp, reportedly has a brother who was denied entry into China earlier this month. In another instance, the nephew of Taiwan's Interior Minister Liu Shyh-fang allegedly lost his job in China in April. Separately, a woman was arrested in California earlier this month over allegations that she spied on President William Lai's son on behalf of Beijing, The Taipei Times reported. Lai, Shen and Liu are members of the DPP, which maintains that Taiwan and the People's Republic of China are separate countries. With the Taipei mayoral election approaching, the report suggested that Beijing's actions could be aimed at undermining Shen's electoral prospects. Earlier polling showed him trailing incumbent Kuomintang (KMT) Mayor Chiang Wan-an by 1.2 percentage points, while subsequent surveys reportedly placed Shen 17 points ahead. Chinese military-affiliated media account Jun Zhengping and the Taiwan Affairs Office also criticised television host Kevin Tsai for attending Shen's campaign event. The ISW warned that even unsuccessful intimidation efforts could discourage public figures from associating with Shen, potentially restricting political debate and influencing Taiwan's electoral environment. Title: "US objective is no more oil, nuclear issues, its total destruction of Iran": Foreign Affairs Expert Waiel Awwad
Description: As crude oil prices surge to USD 117 per barrel and military tensions escalate across West Asia, Foreign Affairs Expert Waiel Awwad has warned that Washington's ultimate objective regarding Iran extends far beyond nuclear negotiations, aiming instead at complete regime change and regional dominance. Speaking with ANI, Awwad asserted that conflicting rhetoric from the White House, ranging from threats to annihilate Iran to proposals for dialogue, reflects a deeper strategic shift aimed at reshaping the Middle East in tandem with Israel. "The United States objective is no more the oil, is no more the nuclear issues... It's a regime change, is the total destruction of Iran, disintegration of Iran, which makes Israel as a dominant force in the region," Awwad told ANI. He added that the posture is also driven by domestic political pressure, stating, "This has also created some sort of a reassessment of the situation to improve his scoring in the American midterm election."Addressing Tehran's retaliatory posture and reports of potential threats to cut Gulf undersea internet cables, the foreign affairs expert emphasised that for Tehran, the conflict has escalated into an "existential war." "For Iran, it has been now an existential war, and for them, threatening that they will cause a global crisis is nothing but to make sure that if the United States goes this time for a war, Iran is prepared fully to defend itself and also to create more hurt to the United States," he noted. He expressed scepticism regarding Washington's diplomatic willingness, pointing out that while Tehran had submitted proposals following the UN General Assembly, the US response remained non-committal. "I don't believe that the United States is serious about the diplomatic outcome of this crisis," he remarked. With crude oil hitting USD 117 per barrel, the highest level since April, Awwad highlighted the growing economic pressures on India's energy security, domestic inflation, and price stability. Commenting on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India and the visit to the strategic Reliance refinery in Jamnagar, Awwad pointed out that Washington is seeking to manoeuvre Venezuelan oil supplies into the global market to offset potential supply shocks. "Jamnagar refinery is not merely a giant factory; in fact, it is one of India's strategic assets, where India can produce more diesel to serve the world and make some kind of balance in the international market," he stated. He cautioned, however, that escalating conflict across maritime choke points like the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb signals a broader geopolitical clash. "It's a war of corridors and the war of dominance in the oil market," he said. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Reliance Industries' Jamnagar facilities in Gujarat on Wednesday, home to the world's largest single-site refinery. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor expressed his privilege at accompanying Rubio to Reliance's Jamnagar facilities. In a post on X, Gor highlighted that India's imports of American liquefied petroleum gas had increased from below 10 per cent to 67 per cent over the preceding year, establishing the United States as India's primary LPG supplier. Furthermore, he drew attention to Reliance's planned investment in constructing a new US oil refinery, characterising the initiative as a significant opportunity to expand American energy production and create jobs. Earlier in the day, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that Iran maintained full control over the Strait of Hormuz, asserting that security was being maintained for vessels operating in the region in accordance with Iranian regulations. The claim came as the IRGC Navy alleged that two supertankers carrying a combined cargo of more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil had struck naval mines while attempting to navigate what Tehran described as an unauthorised southern route through the strategic waterway. Amid the escalating tensions, Iran warned that it would not allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf, challenging Washington's assertions that Iranian military capabilities had been significantly weakened. As per Iranian state broadcaster Press TV, Chief of the General Staff of Iran's Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said Iranian forces had rendered the US Navy ineffective in the region. "The US president must only dream of their military and army entering the Persian Gulf again. They will take this wish to their graves," Abdollahi said. "We will under no circumstances and at no time allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf," he added. Abdollahi also questioned US President Donald Trump's repeated claims that Iran's nuclear facilities had been destroyed, asking why Washington continued to raise concerns about Tehran's nuclear programme if its facilities had already been eliminated. "If you have destroyed everything, then what is the meaning of repeating this delusion?" Abdollahi said, alleging that such statements were intended to mislead public opinion. The latest developments underscore the competing claims by Tehran and Washington over military capabilities, maritime security and the future of energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, amid continued uncertainty over the prospects for a diplomatic agreement. Title: US Treasury proposes expanding investment curbs on Chinese AI, biotech firms
Description: The United States Department of the Treasury has proposed expanding restrictions on American investments in Chinese companies operating in artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology and other advanced technology sectors, citing national security concerns. The proposed measures would also extend the existing investment-control programme to Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia, according to a report by The Epoch Times. The proposal, announced on October 22, seeks to prevent American capital, business expertise and commercial connections from supporting the development of technologies that could strengthen the military, intelligence and surveillance capabilities of countries considered foreign adversaries by Washington, The Epoch Times reported. Under the proposed framework, certain investments would be prohibited, while others would be permitted subject to mandatory reporting to the Treasury Department, generally within 30 days of completion. Ordinary purchases of publicly traded stocks and investment funds would largely remain exempt, subject to specified conditions, the report said. The proposed changes would implement legislation passed by the US Congress in December 2025 to expand the country's existing outbound investment restrictions. However, the new rules have not yet taken effect, and the Treasury Department is accepting public comments until December 7, The Epoch Times reported. The existing programme began in January 2025 under a 2023 presidential executive order, initially targeting selected American investments in Chinese companies involved in AI, semiconductors and quantum technologies. The revised proposal would broaden restrictions on investments in AI companies, including certain transactions that previously required only notification to the Treasury Department. According to The Epoch Times, the department has proposed removing requirements for investors to assess specific technical capabilities or computing-power thresholds of AI systems, arguing that rapid advances in algorithms have made such measurements less reliable. The proposed rules would also strengthen restrictions involving advanced computer chips, quantum technologies, high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Certain investments in companies linked to China's military could face outright prohibitions if the firms, their affiliates or subsidiaries appear on specified US government lists, including lists covering Chinese military companies and biotechnology firms of concern. The Treasury Department estimates that approximately 200 investment transactions annually could fall under the proposed regulations. According to The Epoch Times, the estimate is based on an analysis of around 300 investments made by nearly 230 US-based investors over three years, with an additional adjustment to account for potentially unreported transactions. (ANI)

Title: China accused of pressuring families of Taiwan politicians ahead of key election
Description: China is allegedly stepping up efforts to intimidate relatives of Taiwanese politicians it considers supporters of independence, raising concerns about possible interference in Taiwan's upcoming elections, according to a report by the US-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) and the American Enterprise Institute (AEI), as reported by The Taipei Times. The report suggested that Beijing may be using pressure against family members to discourage politicians and activists from engaging in activities associated with Taiwanese independence. As reported by The Taipei Times, one recent example involves sanctions against VWAY, a company owned by Shen Tu-cheng, the father of Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) legislator and Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. China's Taiwan Affairs Office announced restrictions barring the company from conducting business with Chinese organisations, enterprises and individuals, the Taipei Times reported. Puma Shen was included in Beijing's list of around a dozen people designated as "diehard separatists" in October 2024. According to the report, those named could face severe punishment, including the death penalty, under Beijing's interpretation of its Anti-Secession Law. The report also highlighted other alleged cases of pressure on relatives of Taiwanese public figures. Robert Tsao, founder of United Microelectronics Corp, reportedly has a brother who was denied entry into China earlier this month. In another instance, the nephew of Taiwan's Interior Minister Liu Shyh-fang allegedly lost his job in China in April. Separately, a woman was arrested in California earlier this month over allegations that she spied on President William Lai's son on behalf of Beijing, The Taipei Times reported. Lai, Shen and Liu are members of the DPP, which maintains that Taiwan and the People's Republic of China are separate countries. With the Taipei mayoral election approaching, the report suggested that Beijing's actions could be aimed at undermining Shen's electoral prospects. Earlier polling showed him trailing incumbent Kuomintang (KMT) Mayor Chiang Wan-an by 1.2 percentage points, while subsequent surveys reportedly placed Shen 17 points ahead. Chinese military-affiliated media account Jun Zhengping and the Taiwan Affairs Office also criticised television host Kevin Tsai for attending Shen's campaign event. The ISW warned that even unsuccessful intimidation efforts could discourage public figures from associating with Shen, potentially restricting political debate and influencing Taiwan's electoral environment. (ANI)

Title: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
Description: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11–0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02–0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

Title: Operation Trident: ED arrests six, freezes 1,424 bank accounts, attaches property worth Rs 17.82 Crore
Description: Under multiple-agency 'Operation Trident', the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has frozen 1,424 bank accounts connected to narco-trade and narco-hawala operators in Mizoram and Manipur, arrested six persons and provisionally attached properties worth Rs 17.82 crore belonging to narco-hawala operators based in Mizoram. The action was part of a joint operation carried out by the ED's Aizawl and Imphal sub-zonal offices in coordination with the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the Mizoram Police on October 23. ED's search operation was conducted under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) at multiple premises in Aizawl, Champhai and Lawngtlai (Mizoram) and Churachandpur (Manipur) in three cases of money laundering arising from cross-border trafficking of heroin, brown sugar and methamphetamine tablets from Myanmar and the hawala settlement of the drug proceeds. Besides the ED, parallel action was carried out by the NCB and state police forces jointly at 38 locations in Assam, Mizoram and Manipur against the internation narcotics trafficking network on the same day. ED had earlier secured assets worth Rs 8.19 crore in the form of freezed bank accounts, taking the total assets secured to over Rs 26 crore. Six accused persons were arrested under Section 19 of PMLA during the searches-- three each from Mizoram and Manipur. Production-for-arrest applications against four more accused, presently in judicial custody in narcotics cases, are being processed before the Special Court in Mizoram, the ED said. ED initiated investigations in three cases on the basis of FIRs under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS)Act, 1985. An Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) arises from the seizure of 4.722 kg of heroin (440 soap cases) by Zokhawthar Police, Champhai, on March 14, 2025, being carried from Zokhawthar to Aizawl for a Myanmar-based supplier. Another ECIR arises from the seizure of 49.101 kg of methamphetamine tablets and 40 grams of heroin by the NCB, Agartala, from a convoy on NH-06A near Seling in Mizoram on August 21, 2025, sourced from Chintuang of Myanmar for delivery at the Damchhera-Kanhmun border. However, the third ECIR arises from the seizure of 2.413 kg of brown sugar and cash of Rs 31.43 lakh by Churachandpur Police in Manipur on July 2 this year. In the case, the cash was sale proceeds of drugs supplied from Myanmar, collected at Churachandpur for remittance to the suppliers. ED said its investigation in the three cases has exposed one interconnected narco-hawala ecosystem in which the same set of bank accounts in Champhai, Aizawl and Lawngtlai receive drug money generated in Manipur, Mizoram, Assam and Tripura and settle it with suppliers in Myanmar. The North-East, sharing a 1,643 km porous border with Myanmar, has emerged as the principal land corridor for drugs produced in the Golden Triangle, which India now terms the 'Death Triangle'.  Officials said that Heroin and methamphetamine tablets entering Mizoram and Manipur are consumed locally and moved onward through Assam to the rest of India and Bangladesh, and the drug money generated across this chain flows back to the border towns of Mizoram for settlement with the Myanmar-based suppliers. According to local sources, security forces allegedly detained four young men during a raid at Kohad Bazaar, after which their whereabouts became unknown. Adeel was reportedly among them. Another resident, Mushtaq, son of Master Sudeer, was allegedly taken away from the same locality. The recovery followed the discovery of two more bodies in Buleda, Kech district. The victims were identified as Mehran Baloch and 19-year-old student Yasir.The Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) stated that Mehran had been detained during a raid on his home on November 16, 2025, while Yasir was allegedly taken from his residence on March 2, 2026. Both had reportedly remained missing since their detention. The alleged killings come amid broader concerns over civilian deaths in the province. According to the BYC's report covering January to June 2026, 150 civilians were killed, including 15 minors. The organisation attributed 48 deaths to what it described as the "kill and dump" practice and alleged that 20 others resulted from staged encounters. Human rights and political groups have repeatedly accused Pakistani authorities of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings in Balochistan, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. They say thousands of people remain missing and have urged the United Nations and international human rights organisations to intervene. Separately, the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) continued its protest outside the Quetta Press Club for the 6,397th consecutive day, as reported by The Balochistan Post. (ANI)

Description: Highlighting India's transformative strides across digital public health, deep-tech research, and grassroots agriculture, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday announced that the national telemedicine initiative 'E-Sanjeevani' has achieved a historic milestone of nearly 50 crore (500 million) tele-consultations. Addressing the 139th episode of his monthly radio broadcast, 'Mann Ki Baat', the Prime Minister spotlighted groundbreaking scientific work at IIT Madras-where researchers are conducting a world-first 3D mapping of the human brain using the Param Shakti supercomputer-while also applauding inspiring grassroots efforts in Meghalaya and Nagaland that have revived traditional millet cultivation through value addition and community participation. Commending the digital transformation in healthcare delivery, PM Modi said, "The 'E-Sanjeevani Programme' shows how technology can improve lives and make everyday tasks easier. It gives me great satisfaction to see that, through this, about 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted so far. It is an excellent example of the power of technology, the spirit of service of our doctors, and the trust of our fellow citizens. Today, through its vast network, the E-Sanjeevani service has reached even remote parts of the country." He noted that over 1.9 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have brought accessible primary medical care directly to panchayat levels. "Earlier, even a routine doctor's visit could take up much of one's time. Today, nearly 1.9 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are improving healthcare access. These Arogya Mandirs are evolving into wellness centres for local panchayats. Most heartening is that the villagers are now getting regular health check-ups. E-Sanjeevani is playing a vital role in this transformation," the Prime Minister said. Spotlighting landmark achievements in deep tech and science, PM Modi lauded the 'Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre' at IIT Madras for developing a world-first brain imaging technology platform. "Through this, high-resolution digital 3D pictures of the human brain are being prepared. Their aim is to do 3D mapping of 100 human brains and study them in detail in the coming days. This is the first mission of its kind in the entire world. Param Shakti supercomputer is being used in this work. The country's industry, along with the government, has played a big role in the construction of this brain centre. Many alumni of IIT and academia have also come together for this research centre," he noted. Turning attention to the Northeast, the Prime Minister shared inspiring stories of youth-led innovation and the revival of traditional crops. He highlighted Khanduli village in Meghalaya's West Jaintia Hills, where two friends reversed the decline in millet farming through commercial value addition. "They focused on creating new products from millets. Through value addition, they developed items such as cookies, cakes, and muffins, as well as baby food made from millets. This led to an increase in the sales of millet-based products and a subsequent rise in the demand for millets," he said. PM Modi also praised Chekjing Sangma, a farmer from Sadolpara in Meghalaya's West Garo Hills, for adopting modern farming methods to cultivate millets, thereby boosting income and spreading community awareness. He further highlighted Kezoma village in Kohima, Nagaland, where millet farming was resurrected after a decade-long hiatus. "In Kezoma, the cultivation of millets had ceased there for over a decade, leaving an entire generation unfamiliar with this traditional crop... In 2024, the local community resumed the cultivation of millets, and in 2025, Kezoma celebrated its first-ever millet festival," he said. Emphasising the spirit of service and empathy, the Prime Minister commended the family of Shivani from Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, who took the courageous decision of organ donation after she tragically succumbed to a road accident. "One such act of humanity can bring happiness back into another family. At the same time, it can also make a valuable contribution in research," he remarked. Looking ahead to October 31, PM Modi paid tribute to Punjab-born scientist Dr. Narinder Singh Kapany on his upcoming centenary birth anniversary. "He is known to the world as the 'Father of Fibre Optics'... It is difficult to even imagine the era of the internet and digital communication in which we live today without fibre optics. On this occasion, we pay our respects to Narinder Singh Kapany. I would like our youth to read about and learn from scientists like him, and draw inspiration from them," he stated. Noting that October 31 also marks the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, observed nationwide as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day), the Prime Minister urged citizens to participate widely in the annual 'Run for Unity'. "The Run for Unity is an opportunity to strengthen our unity and renew our commitment to the nation. I urge all of you to take part in the Run for Unity with great enthusiasm," he said. The broadcast drew wide listenership across the country. In Lucknow, BJP National General Secretary Vinod Tawde tuned into the programme, while Karnataka BJP State President B.Y. Vijayendra listened to the address in Bengaluru. In Patna, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary attended a broadcast screening alongside citizens. The Prime Minister highlighted milestones such as Bihar's Purnia makhana reaching Greece and Karnataka's Kalaburagi pulses entering the Maldives, while urging citizens to consciously prioritise locally crafted goods during the upcoming festive season of Diwali and Chhath to accelerate the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India). "During this festive season, you must all have noticed a change around you. Now people have started giving a lot of importance to indigenous products while shopping. This spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is taking our products to markets around the world," PM Modi said. (ANI)

Title: "Spirit of 'Vocal for Local' taking Indian products to world markets": PM Modi in 139th 'Mann Ki Baat'
Description: Asserting that the growing public embrace of indigenous goods is propelling Indian produce onto the global stage, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said that the spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is successfully opening up international markets for the country's farmers and rural artisans. Addressing the 139th episode of his 'Mann Ki Baat', the Prime Minister highlighted milestones such as Bihar's Purnia makhana reaching Greece and Karnataka's Kalaburagi pulses entering the Maldives, while urging citizens to consciously prioritise locally crafted goods during the upcoming festive season of Diwali and Chhath to accelerate the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India). "During this festive season, you must all have noticed a change around you. Now people have started giving a lot of importance to indigenous products while shopping. This spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is taking our products to markets around the world," PM Modi said. Citing concrete examples of local produce finding international acclaim, he said, "Makhana (foxnut) from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece. 'Arhar dal' from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is now going to the Maldives, which means new markets are opening up in the world for the farmers of India." The Prime Minister also commended tribal communities in Maharashtra for blending traditional craftsmanship with modern market requirements through initiatives like 'Shabri Naturals'. "Tribal communities in Maharashtra have focused a lot on the packaging of the products they make. Here, through 'Shabri Naturals', products made from honey, Mahua, Chir, and bamboo are being brought into the market. There is an imprint of tribal art on their packaging. You will be happy to know that this packaging has received Japan's prestigious 'Good Design Award'," he said. Underlining the resurgence of Khadi and handicraft sectors, PM Modi stated that the growing popularity of Khadi is directly empowering skilled artisans across the nation. With festivals around the corner, he made a personal appeal to consumers to embrace domestic craftsmanship. "During festivals, we buy many things for our families and loved ones. This time too, when you shop, please prioritise products made by local artisans. Your purchases will encourage them. This affinity of yours will take the 'Vocal for Local' campaign further, and the further the 'Vocal for Local' campaign advances, the faster the dream of Atmanirbhar Bharat will be realised," the Prime Minister remarked. Touching upon the importance of sanitation ahead of Diwali and Chhath, PM Modi called upon citizens to participate actively in cleanliness initiatives. "The sacred festivals of Diwali and Chhath are just a few days away. For this, cleanliness campaigns are being run from place to place. We must keep those places clean where we live. Our small efforts can only bring big changes around us," he said. The 139th episode of the monthly broadcast was tuned into by leaders and citizens across the country. In Bhubaneswar, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi listened to the address, while in Ranchi, Jharkhand, BJP leaders including Union Minister Annapurna Devi and party leader Nitin Nabin joined locals to listen to the Prime Minister's broadcast. Earlier in the day, recalling the beginning of 'Mann Ki Baat' 12 years ago, on the occasion of Vijayadashami, the Prime Minister said the programme had continued uninterrupted, with listeners playing an important role throughout the journey. "12 years ago, on the auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami, we began 'Mann Ki Baat'. Since then, our journey has continued uninterrupted. All of you have been both fellow travellers and guides on this journey. For me, 'Mann Ki Baat' has been a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the hard work, courage, commitment, dedication and spirit of service of the common man of our country," PM Modi said. Drawing a parallel with India's centuries-old tradition of pilgrimages, he said, "Our country has had a tradition of pilgrimages for centuries, adding, "For me, 'Mann Ki Baat' is no less than a pilgrimage, a journey to closely understand the efforts of people of the country and to pay tribute to their contributions." (ANI)

Description: The Israeli Air Force, in coordination with the Shin Bet security agency, eliminated two commanders of Hamas' military wing in separate airstrikes in the Gaza Strip last week, accusing the terror group of systematically violating the ceasefire, the Israeli Air Force said. In a post on X, the Israeli Air Force said, "The Air Force and Shin Bet attacked two days ago (Saturday) in the Gaza City area in the southern Gaza Strip and eliminated the terrorist Muhammad Khalawa, a commander in the military intelligence array of the military wing of the Hamas terror organisation. In an additional strike last week (Thursday), the Air Force attacked and eliminated the terrorist Ahmed Zaher Fouad Abu-Udeh, an engineering commander in the military wing of the Hamas terror organisation." "Throughout the war and particularly in recent times, the terrorists advanced terror infrastructures against IDF forces and the citizens of the State of Israel and acted to restore the capabilities of the Hamas terror organisation, while systematically violating the ceasefire," the Israeli Air Force said. It added that the two men were targeted from the air to remove the threats they posed. "Security forces are deployed in the area in accordance with the agreement and will continue to act to remove any threat," the Air Force said. Separately, the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), alongside the Israel Border Police and the Israel Security Agency, conducted counter-terrorism operations across Judea and Samaria over the weekend, resulting in the arrest of 40 suspects. In an operational update on X, the IDF said its forces operated in around 40 areas and 400 locations, focusing on areas associated with Hamas. The military said those arrested included individuals affiliated with Hamas and Islamic Jihad, as well as suspects involved in incitement, public disorder and stone-throwing. The IDF also reported launching a targeted operation in the Hebron area following an attack on Friday that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded additional personnel. According to the military, the operation aimed to dismantle terrorist infrastructure and prevent further attacks. It said civilians were permitted to temporarily leave the area through designated screening points and that no civilians were forced to evacuate. Title: China-aligned hackers used AI tool to target over 2,250 cloud environments worldwide
Description: A China-aligned hacking group used an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to accelerate cyberattacks against hundreds of organisations worldwide, including an incident involving US technology company ConnectWise, according to a report by The Epoch Times (TET). Citing findings published by Microsoft on October 21, the report said the hacking group Storm-0940, which Microsoft has tracked since 2021, compromised credentials associated with ConnectWise's Cloud Backup application. The stolen credentials potentially enabled attackers to exploit access already authorised by customers using Microsoft's cloud services. The group reportedly used ARTEX, a Chinese-developed AI security-testing tool, to automate scanning, password attempts and exploitation of application permissions. Its targets included government agencies, defence contractors, financial institutions, technology companies and other organisations. According to the TET report, Storm-0940 attempted to access more than 2,250 customer cloud environments through compromised ConnectWise applications. Microsoft clarified that this figure represented attempted access, not confirmed breaches. In several cases, the attackers obtained privileged access to cloud systems in less than three hours after initial targeting. Microsoft observed the group examining cloud resources, modifying application credentials and attempting to change permissions. Such changes could allow unauthorised access to persist even after the original compromised credentials were disabled. However, Microsoft noted that successful access did not necessarily mean customer data had been stolen. ConnectWise confirmed unauthorised access to credentials associated with its Cloud Backup service, formerly known as SkyKick. In an October 25 update, the company said existing backup archives remained encrypted, isolated and preserved, with no indication they had been compromised. It also reported no evidence that other ConnectWise products or services were affected. The incident disrupted access to Cloud Backup while investigations and restoration work continued. ConnectWise planned to begin allowing partners to restore data from existing backups on October 26, followed by phased re-enrolment. Customers were advised to keep affected application connections disabled until restoration instructions arrived and to check their Microsoft 365 environments for suspicious activity. As cited by TET, ARTEX was originally developed to help security professionals identify weaknesses in computer systems. The tool uses AI to plan operations, direct other tools and pursue different ways into networks with limited human intervention. Microsoft said the automation enabled Storm-0940 to conduct operations simultaneously and exploit stolen credentials rapidly. Its researchers warned that the speed of the activity left defenders with very little time to respond to alerts. The report noted that ARTEX had previously been identified in attacks involving South Korean financial institutions and Japanese companies. Japanese investigators reportedly found the tool on six overseas servers targeting approximately 80 businesses. Microsoft did not attribute those earlier attacks to Storm-0940. According to TET, ARTEX creator Autumn-27 condemned the tool's misuse in an October 8 statement, denied involvement in the reported attacks and announced that public updates and maintenance would end. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook said on October 16 that ARTEX began as a personal project by its RedAgents product lead. The company acknowledged misuse of the open-source version in major financial-sector security incidents and said it lacked built-in security controls. TET reported that it contacted ThreatBook, Microsoft and ConnectWise for further comment, but none had responded by publication time. (ANI)

Title: China-aligned hackers used AI tool to target over 2,250 cloud environments worldwide
Description: A China-aligned hacking group used an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to accelerate cyberattacks against hundreds of organisations worldwide, including an incident involving US technology company ConnectWise, according to a report by The Epoch Times (TET). Citing findings published by Microsoft on October 21, the report said the hacking group Storm-0940, which Microsoft has tracked since 2021, compromised credentials associated with ConnectWise's Cloud Backup application. The stolen credentials potentially enabled attackers to exploit access already authorised by customers using Microsoft's cloud services. The group reportedly used ARTEX, a Chinese-developed AI security-testing tool, to automate scanning, password attempts and exploitation of application permissions. Its targets included government agencies, defence contractors, financial institutions, technology companies and other organisations. According to the TET report, Storm-0940 attempted to access more than 2,250 customer cloud environments through compromised ConnectWise applications. Microsoft clarified that this figure represented attempted access, not confirmed breaches. In several cases, the attackers obtained privileged access to cloud systems in less than three hours after initial targeting. Microsoft observed the group examining cloud resources, modifying application credentials and attempting to change permissions. Such changes could allow unauthorised access to persist even after the original compromised credentials were disabled. However, Microsoft noted that successful access did not necessarily mean customer data had been stolen. ConnectWise confirmed unauthorised access to credentials associated with its Cloud Backup service, formerly known as SkyKick. In an October 25 update, the company said existing backup archives remained encrypted, isolated and preserved, with no indication they had been compromised. It also reported no evidence that other ConnectWise products or services were affected. The incident disrupted access to Cloud Backup while investigations and restoration work continued. ConnectWise planned to begin allowing partners to restore data from existing backups on October 26, followed by phased re-enrolment. Customers were advised to keep affected application connections disabled until restoration instructions arrived and to check their Microsoft 365 environments for suspicious activity. As cited by TET, ARTEX was originally developed to help security professionals identify weaknesses in computer systems. The tool uses AI to plan operations, direct other tools and pursue different ways into networks with limited human intervention. Microsoft said the automation enabled Storm-0940 to conduct operations simultaneously and exploit stolen credentials rapidly. Its researchers warned that the speed of the activity left defenders with very little time to respond to alerts. The report noted that ARTEX had previously been identified in attacks involving South Korean financial institutions and Japanese companies. Japanese investigators reportedly found the tool on six overseas servers targeting approximately 80 businesses. Microsoft did not attribute those earlier attacks to Storm-0940. According to TET, ARTEX creator Autumn-27 condemned the tool's misuse in an October 8 statement, denied involvement in the reported attacks and announced that public updates and maintenance would end. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook said on October 16 that ARTEX began as a personal project by its RedAgents product lead. The company acknowledged misuse of the open-source version in major financial-sector security incidents and said it lacked built-in security controls. TET reported that it contacted ThreatBook, Microsoft and ConnectWise for further comment, but none had responded by publication time. (ANI)

Title: Sudan: One Year on from the Cataclysm of El Fasher
Description: Click to expand Image Displaced women and girls walk through the vast IDP site in Tawila, Sudan, February 23rd, 2026.  2026 Giles Clarke/Avaaz via Getty Images "It is as if a tsunami had hit the city,"said a resident who returned to Sudan's El Fasher only to find it destroyed and largely abandoned after the Rapid Support Forces' (RSF) October 2025 takeover. For 18 months, the RSF laid siege to the city, digging a trench around it in its final months, forcing starving residents to survive on animal fodder, until even that ran out. In the siege's final weeks, the RSF increasingly used drones to target government soldiers, aligned armed groups, and civilians who were ensnared in a tiny area, leaving many maimed or dead. During the last days of the offensive, the RSFcommitted multiple massacres. The UN Human Rights Officeestimates over 6,000 people were killed in just three days. RSF fighters also committed widespread sexual violence against women and girls and ran a massive abduction-for-ransom racket, killing those who couldn't pay. Thousands of civilians may still languish in RSF dungeons. Colombian private military contractors trained in UAE military baseswere deployed alongside the RSF on the front lines, operating drones and artillery. Survivors' accounts confirm the contractors were present during some of the worst atrocities. TheUN fact-finding mission on Sudan concluded that the RSF campaign bore the "hallmarks of genocide," adding to an increasingly damning body of evidence of the RSF's serious crimes. Governments did not act to prevent these atrocities. In the aftermath, several governmentsformed a coalition to prevent further atrocities and promote justice in Sudan, and they now need to act together to meet survivors' demands that those responsible be brought to justice. One year on, RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo "Hemedti" has not even been sanctioned -bar previously by the President Biden administration - despite the crimes of his fighters. The Global Security Services Group (GSSG), the UAE-based company that apparently hired the Colombian fighters, has not faced sanctions, nor is the UAE being held accountable for its military support to the RSF, notwithstanding it violates the UN arms embargo on Darfur. At the UN Security Council, the US is pushing for a countrywide extension of the arms embargo. Yet the existing UN arms and sanctions regime has only been renewed for a few months, and the publication of its Panel of Experts' latest reporthas been delayed. Unlike tsunamis, the horrors of El Fasher were preventable. One year on, global actors should ensure it never happens again, take bold steps to protect civilians, and hold those responsible to account.
